finalReport:
# OpenCode × OpenCut Integration — Technical Feasibility Today

## Verdict

**A *stable* OpenCode integration around OpenCut is not feasible today.** What is feasible today is a fragile, lab-only workaround: pin a patched classic fork, drive it via a Playwright `page.evaluate()` MCP bridge, and accept browser-local storage, in-browser export, and commit-pinned schema.

This is not a licensing or OpenCode-protocol problem. It is an OpenCut automation-surface + stability problem.

- **Verified fact:** OpenCut is split: usable classic line plus incomplete ground-up rewrite where Editor API, MCP server, headless mode and Rust core are roadmap, not present ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md), [rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811), [classic archived](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).
- **Verified fact:** Classic timeline work is in-process only via `EditorCore`/`TimelineManager`, no stable external API ([timeline concept](https://mintlify.wiki/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/concepts/timeline), [EditorCore](https://mintlify.wiki/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/concepts/editor-core)).
- **Verified fact:** No stable upstream CLI/API/MCP/headless today ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)).
- **Workaround (verified to exist, not stable):** Community Playwright bridges requiring patched local classic ([161-tool controller](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller), [bridge pattern](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP), [fork-pinned 12-tool server](https://github.com/kenimo49/opencut-mcp)).
- **Roadmap (not buildable today):** Rust core engine + Editor API + plugin host + headless + MCP + scripting + GPUI desktop ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
- **Uncertainty / partial:** Versioned JSON file contract with `schema_version` exists only as unmerged PR ([PR #764](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/764)); synthesis of feasible vs preferred architecture is inference from blocking evidence, marked PARTIAL.

## 1. Editor state & timeline manipulation

**Verified fact:** Maintainers state “OpenCut is being rewritten from the ground up” with Editor API, plugin-first architecture, Rust core, MCP server, headless mode and scripting tab as “What’s coming” ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)). The previous version at `opencut-app/opencut-classic` is “the one to reach for today” ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)), now archived and “no longer maintained” ([classic](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).

**Verified fact:** Classic model is `Scene -> Tracks (video/audio/text/sticker) -> Elements`, managed in-process by `TimelineManager` (tracks/elements, editing ops, batch updates, preview commit/discard, clipboard) ([timeline](https://mintlify.wiki/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/concepts/timeline)). State is centralized in `EditorCore` singleton with managers for timeline, playback, scenes, project, media, renderer, save, audio, selection, command, accessed via `getInstance()` / `useEditor()`, e.g. `editor.timeline.addTrack()` ([EditorCore](https://mintlify.wiki/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/concepts/editor-core)).

**Inference:** Do not build against `main` rewrite expecting an editor; build-or-pin classic if you must build today.

## 2. Persistence

**Verified fact:** Projects live locally in browser: IndexedDB for project data/metadata, local storage for preferences, “all data stays on your device,” offline-capable ([project management](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/features/project-management)). `StorageService` splits `IndexedDBAdapter<SerializedProject>` + media metadata vs `OPFSAdapter` for media bytes, later per-project (`video-editor-media-{projectId}` / `media-files-{projectId}`) ([storage commit](https://github.com/realtgy/OpenCut/commit/09373eb4a3f792d96d97d81f4fb86539d76e5702)).

**Verified fact:** There is no portable/versioned project file in upstream; “Projects are locked in IndexedDB/OPFS” with “no way to programmatically generate an editing project” ([issue #719](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719)).

**Implication for OpenCode:** OpenCode cannot write a file and hand it to OpenCut. It must either drive live browser state or rely on unmerged export/import.

## 3. Media storage

**Verified fact:** Same split as above: OPFS for bytes, IndexedDB for metadata ([storage commit](https://github.com/realtgy/OpenCut/commit/09373eb4a3f792d96d97d81f4fb86539d76e5702)). OPFS needs File System Access API; Safari before macOS 14.4 hides it behind flags, fallback is in-memory/IndexedDB, must serve over https/localhost ([OPFS Safari FAQ](https://opencut.dev/faq/opencut-opfs-safari/)).

**Implication:** Headless Chromium choice matters; Safari path is not automation-grade. Media ingest must go through hidden file-input / `setInputFiles` style workarounds in forks, not a stable upload API.

## 4. Rendering / export

**Verified fact:** `RendererManager.exportProject({format, quality, fps, includeAudio, onProgress, onCancel}) -> {success, buffer, error, cancelled}`, coordinating `CanvasRenderer` + `SceneExporter` ([RendererManager](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/renderer-manager)). Supported outputs are MP4 (H.264) and WebM (VP9) with Low/Medium/High/Very High presets, default MP4 high with audio ([export docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/features/export)).

**Verified fact (context):** WebCodecs path with MediaRecorder fallback where encoders missing is the documented resilience pattern; export still runs inside the browser and returns a buffer for download, not a headless CLI artifact.

**Inference:** Do not promise server-side batch rendering today; export requires a live browser with WebCodecs and project media already in OPFS/IndexedDB.

## 5. Automation surface, process boundary, MCP/API status

**Verified fact — no upstream surface:** MCP server and headless mode are “What’s coming” ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)), unchecked in rewrite plan alongside Editor API, plugin API/host, scripting ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

**Verified fact — workarounds only:**
- 161-tool MCP via Playwright injecting into browser, requires legacy Next.js App Router classic + patch script ([controller](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)).
- Pattern is `headless Chromium -> page.evaluate() -> EditorCore methods + Zustand stores` via `window.__opencut / window.__stores`; project data stays in IndexedDB/OPFS, no server storage ([bridge](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP)).
- Minimal 12-tool variant targets `kenimo49/opencut-classic` fork (not archived upstream) exposing `window.__editor` + MediaTime helpers, wrapping Timeline/Media/Renderer managers; compat is commit-pinned, with quirks (empty tracks pruned, MediaTime integer ticks) ([fork MCP](https://github.com/kenimo49/opencut-mcp)).

**Verified fact — process boundary:** You must run the classic web app locally (e.g. `localhost:3000/3001` pattern in those bridges) with patched globals; production hosted app does not expose hooks. This is a same-machine browser + Node MCP sidecar, not a service API.

## 6. Desktop availability

**Verified fact:** `apps/desktop` native app built with GPUI is “(in progress)” and “opt-in … skip unless working on desktop,” needing Rust toolchain + native deps ([desktop README snapshot](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/f5f31b43df9ef46f1afdd63ba759b2f9bd80e7a3/README.md)). Desktop UI (GPUI), Android/iOS, public beta are unchecked roadmap ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

**Inference:** Do not target desktop for automation; target pinned classic web + Chromium.

## 7. OpenCode side

**Verified fact:** OpenCode is an MCP client supporting stdio and SSE, discovering via `ListTools` and namespacing `{server}_{tool}` ([OpenCode MCP docs](https://opencode-ai-opencode.mintlify.app/features/mcp-integration)). Protocol-wise it can consume a local stdio bridge like the controllers above.

**Inference:** OpenCode is the easy side; OpenCut stability is the blocker.

## 8. Backward compat / schema stability

**Verified fact:** No guarantee. Classic is archived/unmaintained ([classic](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)). Storage has v0-to-v27 migration chain with runner/transformers ([migration refactor](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/commit/f5f31b43df9ef46f1afdd63ba759b2f9bd80e7a3)), and migrations have broken timeline data requiring repair (“repair scene tracks broken by v23-to-v24 migration”) ([migration fix](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/commit/6312fc5b078689bc82c52fda9b7f92ee0a21d311)).

**Partial / uncertainty:** PR #764 adds versioned JSON export/import with `schema_version`, excluding blobs, new ID on import, but review notes no published versioned JSON Schema and importer trusts file without migration ([PR #764](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/764)). Do not treat this as stable contract until merged + schema published + migration-tested.

## 9. Licensing

**Verified fact (non-blocking):** OpenCut MIT (use/copy/modify/merge/publish/distribute/sublicense/sell with notice, AS-IS) ([OpenCut LICENSE](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/LICENSE)). OpenCode MIT same permissive grant ([OpenCode LICENSE](https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode/blob/main/LICENSE)). User owns created content, free for personal/commercial/client work ([terms](https://opencut.app/terms)).

**Inference:** Fork-patch-pin route is legally permitted; “AS-IS, no warranty” reinforces no stability promise.

## 10. Feasible-today architecture (fragile, lab-only)

Use only if you accept pinning and breakage:

```
OpenCode (MCP client, stdio)
  -> community MCP sidecar (e.g. fork-pinned 12-tool or 161-tool controller)
    -> Playwright headless Chromium
      -> page.evaluate() -> window.__editor/__opencut (patched classic fork @ pinned commit)
        -> EditorCore.TimelineManager / MediaManager / RendererManager -> IndexedDB+OPFS -> in-browser export buffer -> copy out via sidecar
```

Rules: pin both repos by commit ([fork MCP](https://github.com/kenimo49/opencut-mcp) pattern); run local classic only; Chromium with WebCodecs, not Safari ([OPFS FAQ](https://opencut.dev/faq/opencut-opfs-safari/)); handle MediaTime ticks, track-pruning, hidden file-input quirks; version your own DraftTemplate shim because upstream has none ([issue #719](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719)); expect breakage on any upstream pull.

## 11. Preferred future architecture (do not build yet)

Wait for or contribute to:

```
OpenCode -> first-party OpenCut MCP server / headless CLI -> Rust core engine (same as UI)
  + stable Editor API + plugin host
  + versioned DraftTemplate <-> SerializedProject contract with JSON Schema + migrations (successor to PR #764)
  + headless batch rendering (no browser), proper media ingest, desktop/mobile from one core
```

Blocking checklist maps directly to unchecked rewrite items ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)): engine/UI separation, Editor API design, headless mode, MCP server, project storage, scripting.

## 12. Blocking evidence (what would change the verdict)

1. First-party Editor API + MCP + headless move from “What’s coming” to present ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md), [tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
2. Published versioned project JSON Schema + migration guarantee to replace “locked in IndexedDB/OPFS” ([issue #719](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719)) and unmerged `schema_version` ([PR #764](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/764)).
3. No-archived-target: maintained line with compat policy to replace archived classic ([classic](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)) and v0-v27 churn/breakage ([migration refactor](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/commit/f5f31b43df9ef46f1afdd63ba759b2f9bd80e7a3), [fix](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/commit/6312fc5b078689bc82c52fda9b7f92ee0a21d311)).
4. Stable desktop or explicit “web-only automation” decision to replace in-progress GPUI ([desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/f5f31b43df9ef46f1afdd63ba759b2f9bd80e7a3/README.md)).

Until then: prototype only on a fork-pinned bridge; do not ship “stable OpenCode integration.”

## Research limitations
- Reportable claim claim-0011 is PARTIAL: Versioned JSON project export/import with schema_version (PR #764) is the candidate stable file contract but remains unmerged and lacks published versioned JSON Schema and migration handling.
- Reportable claim claim-0013 is PARTIAL: Synthesis: a stable OpenCode integration around OpenCut is not feasible today without fork-pinning to a patched classic plus Playwright bridge; feasible-today is fragile lab-only, preferred-future is Rust core + stable Editor API + first-party MCP/headless + versioned DraftTemplate/SerializedProject contract.
finalResponse:
Research completed in 1m 50s · 50 citations · 12 searches

Scope: stable OpenCode integration around OpenCut — editor/timeline, persistence/media/export, automation/process/desktop/MCP, schema stability, licensing.

Findings: Stable integration is **not feasible today**. OpenCut is split between archived classic (usable) and incomplete rewrite where Editor API, MCP, headless, Rust core are roadmap. Classic timeline is in-process `EditorCore/TimelineManager` only; persistence is browser-local IndexedDB+OPFS with no portable file; export is in-browser MP4/WebM; no upstream CLI/API/MCP; only Playwright `page.evaluate()` bridges on patched forks work; desktop GPUI is in-progress; schema has v0-v27 churn with real breakage. Licensing MIT+MIT is non-blocking.

Feasible-today: pin patched classic fork + Playwright MCP sidecar + Chromium, lab-only. Preferred-future: Rust core + stable Editor API + first-party MCP/headless + versioned JSON contract.

Uncertainty: versioned JSON `schema_version` PR #764 unmerged without published schema; overall feasibility synthesis is PARTIAL inference.

claimSummaries.statement: Classic timeline manipulation is in-process only via EditorCore singleton and TimelineManager (Scene->Tracks->Elements, commands/undo), with no stable upstream external programmatic API.
Persistence is browser-local only (IndexedDB for project/metadata, OPFS for media bytes, per-project adapters) with no server-side storage and no stable portable project file in upstream.
Media bytes live in OPFS with IndexedDB metadata; OPFS requires File System Access API and falls back to memory/IndexedDB on Safari, constraining headless/browser choice.
Rendering/export is in-browser via RendererManager/CanvasRenderer/SceneExporter (mediabunny/WebCodecs) to MP4/WebM with quality presets, plus MediaRecorder fallback where encoders missing.
Upstream OpenCut exposes no stable CLI, REST API, MCP server, or headless mode today; those are explicitly listed as coming in rewrite tracking.

Only working automation today is community Playwright page.evaluate bridges (161-tool controller, RavenMeld bridge, kenimo 12-tool fork) requiring a patched local classic editor exposing window.__opencut/__stores/__editor.
Desktop (GPUI native, apps/desktop) is in-progress and opt-in, not a stable automation target.
OpenCode can consume such a bridge as MCP client via stdio/SSE with ListTools discovery, so protocol compatibility is not the blocker.
There is no backward-compat/schema stability guarantee: classic is archived/unmaintained, storage has v0-v27 migration churn, and migrations have broken timeline data (v23-v24 fix).
Versioned JSON project export/import with schema_version (PR #764) is the candidate stable file contract but remains unmerged and lacks published versioned JSON Schema and migration handling.
Licensing is non-blocking: OpenCut MIT and OpenCode MIT permit use/modify/fork/commercial integration; user owns content, software AS-IS.

Synthesis: a stable OpenCode integration around OpenCut is not feasible today without fork-pinning to a patched classic plus Playwright bridge; feasible-today is fragile lab-only, preferred-future is Rust core + stable Editor API + first-party MCP/headless + versioned DraftTemplate/SerializedProject contract.
